q: During what period of time in Jewish history did the story of Ruth occur?
a: It occurred in the days when the judges ruled.

q: Why did Elimelek move to Moab with his family?
a: He moved because there was a famine in the land of Judah.

q: What happened to Elimelek in Moab?
a: He died, leaving Naomi a widow.

q: What happened to Naomi’s children in Moab?
a: They died, leaving behind two daughters-in-law for Naomi.

q: Why did Naomi decide to return to Judah?
a: She heard that Yahweh had given the people of Judah food.

q: Where did Naomi want her two daughters-in-law to go?
a: She wanted them to return to their mothers’ houses.

q: What did Naomi want her two daughters-in-law to find?
a: She wanted them to find other husbands.

q: Who did Naomi believe was the source of her trouble?
a: She believed that Yahweh was against her.

q: When Ruth stayed with Naomi, what promise did Ruth make to Naomi?
a: She said, “For I will go to the place where you go, and I will stay in the place where you stay. Your people are my people, and your God is my God.”

q: How long did Ruth say she would remain with Naomi?
a: She said she would remain with Naomi until they died. She said, “In the place where you die, I will die, and there I will be buried. May Yahweh do thus to me, and thus may he add, if death separates between me and between you.”

q: To which town did Naomi return?
a: She returned to Bethlehem.

q: What name did Naomi want to be called and why?
a: She asked to be called “Mara” (which means “bitter”), because she believed that Yahweh had dealt bitterly with her.

q: What time of the year did Naomi and Ruth arrive in Bethlehem?
a: They arrived at the beginning of the barley harvest.

q: What was the relationship between Boaz and Naomi’s dead husband?
a: Boaz was a relative of Naomi’s husband.

q: As Ruth went out to glean for the first time, who did Ruth say she would follow while gleaning grain?
a: She would follow anyone in whose eyes she found favor.

q: What greeting did Boaz give to his workers?
a: He said, “Yahweh be with you.”

q: What did Boaz want to know about Ruth?
a: He wanted to know to whom she belonged.

q: What instructions did Boaz give Ruth concerning her gleaning?
a: He told Ruth not to leave his field, but to stay and work in his field with his female workers.

q: After receiving the favorable instructions, what question did Ruth ask Boaz?
a: She asked Boaz why she had found favor in his sight.

q: What good report had Boaz heard about Ruth?
a: He had heard that Ruth had left her home to follow Naomi.

q: Under whose wings did Boaz say Ruth had found refuge?
a: He said that Ruth had found refuge under Yahweh’s wings.

q: What additional favor did Boaz show to Ruth when they returned to work after mealtime?
a: He allowed Ruth to glean among the bundles.

q: What did Boaz tell his workers to do for Ruth?
a: He commanded the reapers to pull out grain for Ruth from the bundles.

q: When Naomi saw the large amount of grain that Ruth brought back, what question did she ask Ruth?
a: She asked where Ruth had gleaned that day.

q: What blessing did Naomi wish for Boaz when she heard that Boaz had helped Ruth?
a: She said, “May he be blessed by Yahweh.”

q: Why did Naomi think it was good for Ruth to work with Boaz’s women workers?
a: By doing that, Ruth would not come to harm in any other field.

q: What did Ruth do during the rest of the barley harvest?
a: She gleaned with Boaz’s workers and lived with her mother-in-law.

q: What did Naomi say her desire was for Ruth?
a: She desired that Ruth have a place of rest, meaning to have a person who would treat her well.

q: What did Naomi tell Ruth to do before going down to the threshing floor?
a: She told her to wash and anoint herself and to put on her cloak.

q: What was Ruth to do when she went to where Boaz was sleeping?
a: She was to uncover his feet and to lie down there.

q: What was Ruth’s attitude toward Naomi’s instructions?
a: She said she would do everything Naomi told her to do.

q: At midnight, what was Boaz startled to find?
a: He was startled to find that a woman lay at his feet!

q: What was Ruth’s request to Boaz?
a: She asked Boaz to spread his cloak over her, for he was a kinsman-redeemer.

q: Why did Boaz ask a blessing from Yahweh for Ruth?
a: Boaz blessed Ruth because she had come to Boaz, her kinsman-redeemer, rather than pursuing younger men.

q: What did Boaz say he would do about Ruth’s request?
a: He said that he would do all that she asked.

q: What obstacle prevented Boaz from immediately performing the part of a kinsman for Ruth?
a: There was another kinsman-redeemer nearer in relationship than Boaz.

q: How was Boaz going to determine who would act as kinsman for Ruth?
a: If the nearest kinsman-redeemer was willing to redeem Ruth, then Boaz would let him do that. But if he was not willing, then Boaz would be the kinsman-redeemer.

q: Why did Ruth leave the threshing floor early before anyone could recognize her?
a: Boaz did not want people to know that she had been with him overnight at the threshing floor.

q: What gift did Boaz give Ruth before she left the threshing floor?
a: He gave her six large measures of barley.

q: Naomi was sure that Boaz would resolve the issue by what time?
a: He would resolve it by the end of that same day.

q: Where did Boaz go to resolve the issue of who would be the kinsman-redeemer for Ruth?
a: He went to the gate of the city.

q: Who did Boaz ask to sit as witnesses?
a: He asked ten men who were from the elders of the city.

q: What did Boaz first speak about to the other kinsman?
a: He told him that Naomi was selling the piece of land that had been owned by Elimelek.

q: What did Boaz suggest the other kinsman do about the parcel of land?
a: Boaz suggested that the other kinsman could redeem it.

q: What was the other kinsman’s answer?
a: He said he would redeem it.

q: About what additional requirement did Boaz then tell the other kinsman?
a: He told him that he would also have to marry Ruth in order to raise up the name of the dead man over his inheritance.

q: What was the other kinsman’s answer when he learned that he would have to marry Ruth?
a: He said he could not redeem the land.

q: Why did the other kinsman say he could not be the redeemer?
a: He said that it would damage his own inheritance.

q: What did the other kinsman do to show that he agreed that Boaz should be the redeemer?
a: He took off his sandal and gave it to him in front of witnesses.

q: What was the first agreement that Boaz said the elders witnessed?
a: They witnessed that Boaz bought all the land that had belonged to Elimelek.

q: What was the second agreement that Boaz said the elders had witnessed?
a: They had witnessed that Boaz acquired Ruth as his wife.

q: What blessing did the people desire for Boaz?
a: They desired that Yahweh would give him offspring through Ruth, just as Tamar bore a son to Judah.

q: Why did the women say that Ruth was better for Naomi than seven sons?
a: They said this because of Ruth’s love for Naomi, and because Ruth had given birth to a grandson for Naomi.

q: What was Naomi’s relationship with Ruth’s son?
a: Naomi became his nurse or caregiver.

q: What was Ruth’s son’s name?
a: His name was Obed.

q: Of whom was Obed the father and grandfather?
a: Obed was the father of Jesse and the grandfather of David.
